name: AZ-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 partisan lean in a heavily Democratic district
Grijalva's large fundraising and cash advantage
No polling or expert ratings, so forecast rests on fundamentals

model.rationale: The district's D+13 lean, an incumbent Democrat with a roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge, and markets pricing the race around 95% Democratic all point to a safe hold, so the forecast stays at the fundamentals-implied margin with modest uncertainty from the absence of polls.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Grijalva underperforming the district's lean, or a surge of outside spending against her, would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southern Arizona's 7th District is a heavily Democratic seat, and Adelita Grijalva holds it as an incumbent after winning the nomination without difficulty. She has raised over $2.2 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Republican Daniel Butierez has raised only about $224,000 with little cash remaining and no significant outside support on either side. No independent groups are spending meaningfully against her.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on the district's strong Democratic lean, incumbency, and the money gap. Prediction markets put the Democratic candidate's chances around 95%. The seat remains safely Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the lack of direct polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
